questions.question: You can increase your visibility by:

options.text: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: You can increase your visibility by wearing bright or reflective clothing. You can also add extra lights to your motorcycle, use your turn signals, and flash your brake light when needed. These actions help other drivers see you.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
Have only one set of footrests.
Not tell your passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat large enough for two riders. It should also have footrests for your passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear that you wear.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other regulatory signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Goggles will:

options.text: Work as well as a face shield.
Offer the same protection as a windshield.

questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only, not your face. A face shield is better because it protects your whole face. A windshield is not enough protection by itself.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Set up and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
Ride the same way as you would without a passenger.
Tell your passenger the rules after you start riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Set up and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must be properly set up and adjusted to carry a passenger. It needs a large seat and separate footrests for the passenger. You may need to adjust your headlight, tire pressure, and suspension to handle the extra weight.

questions.question: Your best source of information about your motorcycle is:
questions.explanation: Read your owner's manual for information about your specific motorcycle. It has details about how to operate your motorcycle, its specifications, and maintenance.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after drinking one alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drunk riding.
Alcohol will not affect your riding skills.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.explanation: Your body breaks down about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system and affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Shifting into a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.explanation: Shifting into a lower gear slows your motorcycle, similar to braking. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do to stay safe on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on slippery surfaces. Do not make sudden movements, as they can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid a slippery road.

questions.question: Motorcycle signals are:

options.text: Even more important than signals on cars and trucks.
Only needed when another vehicle is next to you.
Less important than signals on cars and trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even more important than signals on cars and trucks.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are more vulnerable than car and truck drivers. So using signals correctly is even more important for motorcyclists.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a good choice for riding clothes?

options.text: A jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles
A baseball cap to cover your hair

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair
questions.explanation: To protect yourself from injury, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: When riding on a bridge grating, what should you do?

options.text: Always ride on the far right side of the lane.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to weave slightly. This is usually not dangerous. Simply relax and cross at a steady speed. Zigzagging to fight the weave is dangerous because it forces you out of your lane.

questions.question: How often should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: To prevent dangerous problems, inspect your motorcycle before every ride. On a motorcycle, small technical issues are more serious than on a car.

questions.question: What can help reduce your chance of crashing?

options.text: Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers
Always stay within a foot of another vehicle

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, always be visible to others. Signal your turns, use your brake light, and position yourself well in the lane. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and to both sides.

questions.question: How does a three-wheeled motorcycle handle curves?

options.text: The same way as a two-wheeled motorcycle
It should not be used in curves
It should use the shoulder when turning

questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or motorcycle with a sidecar corners differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect you from?
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your face from crash injury and from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and rocks thrown up by other vehicles.

questions.question: When should you wear a jacket while riding?

options.text: Only on rides longer than half an hour

questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from the sun and helps prevent dehydration.

questions.question: What is the main active ingredient in marijuana?
questions.explanation: The main active ingredient in marijuana is tetrahydrocannabinol, or THC.

questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention

questions.explanation: To be more visible at an intersection, use your headlight and ride where other drivers can see you clearly. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can escape if needed.

questions.question: When you borrow a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: You don't need to check the tire pressure.
It will handle exactly like your own bike.
The owner will check the brakes, so you don't have to.
Leave extra space between you and other vehicles to have more time to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave extra space between you and other vehicles to have more time to react.
questions.explanation: Check your borrowed motorcycle the same way you check your own. Ride slowly on an unfamiliar bike and keep extra distance when stopping.

questions.question: A driver is tailgating you. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the side so they can share your lane.

questions.explanation: Get the tailgater ahead of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up will only make it more dangerous by encouraging them to tailgate you at higher speeds.

questions.question: When you are stopped behind another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Don't use your rearview mirrors to check traffic behind you.
Look for ways to squeeze through stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay back from the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or another vehicle comes at you too fast from behind.

questions.question: Before riding, check your tires for everything except:
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear.

questions.question: What should you inspect before riding?

options.text: The wear and tread of your tires
How much padding your seat has

questions.correctAnswerText: The wear and tread of your tires
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. Inspect your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.
